description: Statements inside a stored procedure each run in their OWN autocommit transaction - a procedure body does not wrap its statements into one implicit transaction. Three observable consequences: an APPEND_ONLY stream keeps an INSERT even when a later statement deletes the row (one shared transaction would consolidate the pair away and the stream would miss it), a failed statement rolls back only itself and keeps earlier committed work, and an explicit BEGIN TRANSACTION inside the body still suspends autocommit until COMMIT (a STANDARD stream then nets insert+delete of the same row to nothing). Also here: ALTER SESSION at the top level is not transaction-committing DDL, so a second stream read inside the same explicit transaction still shares its window; and an IDENTIFIER() join source sees writes made earlier in the same transaction. Converted 1:1 from features/ProcStatementAutocommitTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE ao_t (id INTEGER, v VARCHAR)
CREATE STREAM ao_s ON TABLE ao_t APPEND_ONLY = TRUE
CREATE TABLE pc_t (id INTEGER NOT NULL)
CREATE STREAM as_s ON TABLE as_t
INSERT INTO sink1 SELECT id FROM as_s
INSERT INTO sink2 SELECT id FROM as_s
CREATE TABLE base_rows (grp_id VARCHAR, v INTEGER)
CREATE STREAM tx_s ON TABLE tx_t
